# View Finder

> View Finder finds scenic, car-reachable high-elevation viewpoints and peaks by combining
> terrain elevation data with OpenStreetMap road and land-use data.

View Finder is a free, single-page web app (also distributed as a desktop app for Windows and
macOS) that overlays elevation data with OpenStreetMap road and land-use data to surface
scenic, drivable high ground. Users pan/zoom a map; the app fetches OpenStreetMap-tagged
viewpoints and summits plus computed elevation local maxima, filters out spots that are on
private or farm land or too far from a road, and ranks the rest by elevation, prominence, and
road-reachability.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/S1xinch/View-Finder): source code, issues, and the
  desktop app releases.
- [Releases](https://github.com/S1xinch/View-Finder/releases/latest): downloadable Windows and
  macOS desktop installers.

## Notes for automated crawlers

- The site is a single page; all functionality lives at the root URL.
- Map data comes from live third-party sources (OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API, an
  OpenTopoData-style elevation service, and OpenFreeMap map tiles) and is not embedded in the
  page's static HTML.
